# SubWorld

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("SubWorld")`

Runs another scene alongside this one and draws it into a texture. Use it for a playable arcade cabinet, a game on a computer inside the game, or a snow globe with its own weather.

`Load` starts the scene that `Scene` names in a world of its own, with its own instances, scripts, physics and clock. Its current camera draws into `view://` followed by `ViewName`, which an `ImageLabel` on a `SurfaceGui` can show.

The two worlds are isolated. A script in one cannot reach an instance in the other. They communicate through `Send` and `Received` on this side, and `SceneService:SendToHost` and `SceneService.HostMessageReceived` inside. This side chooses what input the sub-world receives with `SetInputState`.

A sub-world runs its scene's `ServerScriptService` and `ClientScriptService` as a single-player game, and never the project's `GlobalScriptService`. It ticks once for each tick of this world. At most `[render] max_sub_worlds` run at once (2 by default), and a sub-world cannot contain another. It is not replicated: in a multiplayer match, each machine that loads one runs its own.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Quality` | `Enum.ViewQuality` | `Enum.ViewQuality.Simple` | read/write | How the view is drawn. `Simple` draws without shadows or post-processing effects. `Full` draws the way the main view does. |
| `Resolution` | `Vector2` | `Vector2.new(512, 288)` | read/write | The size of the texture, in pixels, with the same limit as `CameraTexture.Resolution`. |
| `Running` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether the sub-world ticks. When it is off, the world is paused and its picture stays as it was. |
| `Scene` | `string` | — | read/write | The scene file to run, relative to the content folder, such as `scenes/arcade.scene.json`. It is read when `Load` starts the scene; a later change takes effect at the next `Load`. |
| `UpdateInterval` | `number` | `1` | read/write | The number of frames between pictures: at 1 the view is drawn every frame. The world ticks every tick whatever this value is. |
| `ViewName` | `string` | — | read/write | The name of the texture the sub-world is drawn into: it is available as `view://` followed by this name. With an empty name nothing is drawn, and the world still runs. |

## Methods

### `IsLoaded(): boolean`

Returns whether the sub-world's world exists, running or paused. It is true from `Loaded` until `Unload`.

### `Load()`

Starts the scene. It returns at once: the world starts after the current tick, and `Loaded` fires when its scripts have started. Does nothing if the sub-world is already loaded. Raises an error if `[render] max_sub_worlds` are already running, or if it is called inside a sub-world.

### `Send(arguments: ...any)`

Sends values into the sub-world, where `SceneService.HostMessageReceived` fires with them on its next tick. It accepts the values a `RemoteEvent` accepts, except instances, because the two worlds share none. The values are dropped if the sub-world is not loaded.

### `SetInputState(action: string, value: boolean | number | Vector2 | vector)`

Holds the sub-world's `InputAction` named `action` at `value` from its next tick until it is set again. `value` is true or false for a `Bool` action, or a number, a `Vector2` or a `vector` for a direction. No other input reaches the sub-world: the keyboard, mouse and gamepads belong to this world, which decides what to pass on.

### `Unload()`

Stops the sub-world and discards its world, after the current tick. Its picture stays until the next `Load` draws over it. Destroying the `SubWorld` does the same.

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `Loaded()`

Fires when the sub-world's world is running and its scripts have started.

### `Received(arguments: ...any)`

Fires with the values the sub-world passed to `SceneService:SendToHost`, one tick after it sent them.
